questions.a: Heat passing through a solid from the hot end to the cold end, particle to particle.

questions.q: Name two good and two bad conductors of heat.
questions.a: Good: metals like copper, aluminium. Bad: wood, plastic, wool, air.

questions.q: Why do metal handles feel colder than wooden ones in winter?
questions.a: Metal conducts heat away from the hand faster, so it feels colder.
Heat carried by the moving particles of a liquid or gas - hot parts rise, cool parts sink.

questions.q: Why does water in a kettle heat by convection?
questions.a: Warm water at the bottom rises while cooler water sinks, forming currents that spread heat.
Sea breeze, or the upward flight of a hot-air balloon.
Heat travelling as rays without any medium - how the sun's heat reaches earth.

questions.q: Does radiation need a material to travel through?
questions.a: No - it passes even through vacuum of space.

questions.q: Why do we wear light colours in summer?
questions.a: Light colours reflect radiated heat; dark colours absorb it.

concepts.title: Heat, Land, Water and the Cycle of Weather

questions.q: Why do coastal places have milder weather than deserts?
questions.a: Water heats and cools slowly, keeping sea-side temperatures steady; land swings fast.

questions.q: How does land breeze form at night?
questions.a: Land cools faster than the sea; warm air over the sea rises and cooler land air flows to take its place.

questions.q: Why do clouds often form over land in the afternoon near the sea?
questions.a: Warm moist air rises from the heated land and condenses high up into clouds.
